No. If you are arrested, you must be informed “as soon as may be” of the grounds for the arrest, and you have the right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of your choice. (Article 10(1))

There is an exception for arrest or detention under a law providing for preventive detention. In that case, Article 10(1) and (2) do not apply. (Article 10(3))

failing_examples.q39: Article 2A was inserted as a new article and made part of the Constitution by making the Objectives Resolution in the Annex a substantive part of the Constitution. The source says: “The principles and provisions set out in the Objectives Resolution reproduced in the Annex are hereby made substantive part of the Constitution and shall have effect accordingly” (Article 2A). The explicit insertion footnote says: “New Article 2A ins. ibid.” (Article 2A).
